summary: Romania's only origin data on child harm are ANITP's open records of trafficking victims, which give each child's citizenship (285 of 287 child victims in 2025 were Romanian). Police, prosecution and child-protection statistics publish no citizenship or ethnicity, and the census's Roma ethnicity is never linked to crime or victim records.

european_title: Not recorded by any Romanian child-harm source
european_note: Romanian child-harm statistics record citizenship at most. The census records ethnicity, including Roma, but no crime, victim or child-protection statistic does, so neither European descent nor Roma identity can be measured for child harm.
proxy_note: Romania records citizenship only in child-harm data, never ethnicity. Every group below is a proxy, not ethnicity.

harms.label: Child victims of trafficking (ANITP open data)
harms.intro: ANITP identified 707 trafficking victims in 2025, 287 of them children (235 girls). Of the 287 children, 285 were Romanian citizens, 1 Norwegian and 1 Ukrainian. Of all 707 victims, 691 were Romanian and 16 foreign (5 Moldovan, 3 Ukrainian, 3 Sri Lankan, 2 Togolese, 1 Russian, 1 Norwegian, 1 Peruvian). No trafficker data by citizenship.

victims.scope: Romania, child trafficking victims (under 18 at the time of trafficking) identified in 2025
victims.share_note: Computed from ANITP's open dataset 'Set date deschise VTP 2025' (one row per victim; age at trafficking under 18). Citizenship, a proxy, not ethnicity: Romanian citizens include Roma, Hungarians and every other ethnic group, and ANITP records no ethnicity.

cross.text: No perpetrator data by citizenship, so nothing can be linked.

harms.label: Child pornography exploitation of trafficking victims
harms.intro: Of the 287 child trafficking victims, 119 were exploited through child pornography (Art. 374 of the Criminal Code); 118 of them were Romanian citizens. This covers only cases handled as trafficking, not all child sexual abuse material offences.

The Public Ministry's 2025 activity report and the police's published summaries give no citizenship or ethnicity for victims or offenders of violence against children; the police annual statistics file was blocked.
No child-protection statistics by citizenship or ethnicity were found.

ANITP publishes open microdata for every trafficking victim identified in 2025 (707, age, sex, citizenship, exploitation): 287 were children, 285 of them Romanian citizens (1 Norwegian, 1 Ukrainian). Citizenship only; no ethnicity, no trafficker data.
Only child victims of child-pornography exploitation recorded as trafficking victims (119 of the 287 children in ANITP's 2025 microdata) carry citizenship.

components.name: Victim heritage
components.full: Official data by harm that separately identify children of European descent (e.g. White non-Hispanic, White British) alongside every other group, self-reported or official, few unknowns. Broad categories that lump European-descent people with others get partial credit; proxies (nationality, citizenship, migration background, country of birth) at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Perpetrator heritage
components.full: Same standard for perpetrators: not perceived, few unknowns, European descent separately identified. Proxies at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Coverage and missing data
components.full: Over 90% of the population covered, under 10% unknown

components.name: Rates and linkage
components.full: Rates per 100,000 possible, and victim heritage linked to perpetrator heritage

score.gold_standard: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies people of European descent, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when European-descent children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm.
score.rules: Heritage is 75 of every 100 points (victims 37.5, perpetrators 37.5); coverage, rates and access share the other 25. Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most a quarter of the heritage points. A country with no real ethnicity data for victims or perpetrators is capped at 25%.
score.why: Romania scores 8% on the stricter scale (0-20%). Its only origin data are ANITP's open microdata on trafficking victims (age and citizenship for every identified victim). Police, prosecution and child-protection statistics publish no citizenship or ethnicity, the police statistics file was blocked, and the census's Roma ethnicity question is never linked to crime or victim records.
